newsitem.title: INDIA: India cotton weakens after budget lowers duties.
newsitem.headline: India cotton weakens after budget lowers duties.

text.p: Indian cotton prices weakened on Monday due to lower duties proposed in Friday's budget while permission on forward trading failed to provide any sparks, dealers said

"The finance minister in the budget had allowed forward trading in cotton but this announcement had little impact on the market and prices on the other hand remained subdued as the minister had lowered excise duty on synthetic yarn," said Mahesh Thakkar, a leading dealer.
"Cheaper synthetic yarn will lower consumption of cotton," he said.
In spot deals Bengal-deshi slid by five rupees to 805/835 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned fell by 10 rupees to 1,440/1,650 rupees per maund.
Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) however rose by 100 rupees to 11,600/11,800 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) on limited inflow.
Thakkur said after 33 years, the Indian government has allowed forward trading in cotton. "The government had suspended forward trading in cotton way back in 1964," he said.

Though finance minister P. Chidambaram had allowed forward trading in the budget, Thakkur said he expected technical problems at the time of maturity of deliveries as India grows about 112 types of cotton seed.
"First of all we have to restrict tenderable variety as well as types of seed before commencing forward trading in cotton," he added.
